assemblyReasoning.constructionModel: explicit two-sided folded lamina geometry supplies macro curvature; the shader refines only the thin biological margin inside the canonical tip/right/base/left UV domain
assemblyReasoning.orientation: raw UV0 preserves tip=(0.5,1), right=(1,0.5), base=(0.5,0), left=(0,0.5) independently from tiled PBR texture coordinates
assemblyReasoning.interfaces: visible-pass coverage and shadow-caster coverage use the same LeafEdgeCoverage function so foliage and dapple shadows cannot disagree
assemblyReasoning.geometryVsMaterial: fold, size, orientation and attachment remain geometry; sub-centimetre margin irregularity and screen-space edge coverage are material/shader detail
assemblyReasoning.aging: no tears, holes, scorch, storm damage or disaster cues are introduced; edge irregularity represents normal healthy leaf morphology only

scoreTargets.potentialImpact: risk-reduction only until temporal pixels are reviewed

reviewFor: repeated identical serration phase at canopy scale
dapple shadow breakup that reads as card geometry

hardFailRules: Formal foliage materials must use NewTown/FoliageTransmission.
The forward pass must preserve raw canonical UV separately from tiled PBR UV.
The visible pass must use LeafEdgeCoverage and alpha-to-coverage.
The shadow caster must use the same LeafEdgeCoverage function.
Runtime-random edge motion is forbidden for formal still and temporal evidence.
No Visual Fidelity points may be awarded from source-state validation alone.
Any severe edge shimmer, obvious card silhouette or shadow mismatch in real pixels remains a visual FAIL regardless of source QA.
limitations: The underlying lamina still uses the existing coarse generated topology; shader coverage cannot create convex geometry outside that mesh boundary.
Margin phase varies per leaf cluster through the existing deterministic MaterialPropertyBlock, not per individual leaf within a cluster.
Alpha-to-coverage benefit depends on the actual formal render target MSAA state and must be verified in Unity.
Shadow-map filtering, camera distance and grazing angle can still expose aliasing that source inspection cannot predict.
